Pnueli modalities.Research has shown that MITL can be extended with a more general form of counting while preserving decidability [Hirshfeld and Rabinovich, 1999]. This is achieved withPnueli modalities, P nI (φ1, . . . , φk), which specifies that a sequence of events in an interval I must satisfy φ1, . . . , φk in the given order. To highlight their practical utility, we now

General time intervals.In MITL, modalities (temporal operators) decorated withunilateraltime intervals (i.e. time intervals of the form ⟨l,∞ ) or [0, u⟩) can be translated into tester automata without too much difficulty [Raskin and Schobbens, 1997; Geilen, 2003]. However, for practical applications, general time intervals such as ⟨l, u⟩are very handy (see e.g., [Bae and Lee, 2019]). Sect. 4 explains the construction for MITL modalities with general ⟨l, r⟩intervals and the gadgets used for sequentialisation.
